credit._: Decision 809 amended (the coordinator: one alone on the box should feel the town noticed): a resident credits a player in passing for their deed in its town, in place of its hail that day (Main._credit_line): their hand-in there today (hand_in; {count} {item} the reward's words) or a building standing with their goods (built; {item} the good they gave most of, not gold, {building} its name). Each resident once a deed; a_day credits a player a day at most. Voice's words.
hand_in: Heard you brought {count} {item} to the store. Good of you.
Word is you brought the store {count} {item}. That helps.

hand_in_news._: Decision 809: hearsay of a hand-in. A player's first hand-in of a day at a town becomes its news (Main._hand_in_heard, Townsfolk._remember with 'about': them), which residents bring up unasked to other players (Resident.hail_cue's news cue), never to them. lines: voice's words, {name} the player, {count} {item} the reward's counted words.

thanks._: 804, npc's side (Jeff: "nothing happens when I hand things in"): the one who takes a hand-in thanks the player aloud, naming what and how many (Main._thank_aloud on economy's "item" reward; Main._thanker picks who). Lines by trade (voice's words), {count} {item} filled with the reward's words ("3 fish", "a hide", "5 wood and 2 hides"); a trade not listed has the default's; vendor is the stall's keeper by the store (736).
farmer: That's {count} {item} I don't have to find. Thanks.
herder: That's {count} {item} I don't have to find. Thanks.
shepherd: That's {count} {item} I don't have to find. Thanks.

acolyte: Thank you for {count} {item}. It's gladly taken.

keeper._: 807 amended (2) (the coordinator's: chests out of towns): the stall's keeper by each store (736's vendor, Rolf) keeps all hours and the players' lockers. His own lines (voice's words; lore: a plain townsman of the town, never a smith): greet the first time he meets a player, greet_again after; locker when he brings a player's locker out (Main.keeper_locker), nowhere when no free cell beside him is one they can reach (807 amended (6)); back when a player hands starter gear back through his window (807 amended (5): the practice kit retired; no gold, the pieces end).
greet: Store's open. What do you need?
locker: Here's your locker, as you left it.
nowhere: No room to set it down here. Give me a bit of space and ask again.
back: I'll take that back. Can't pay for it, mind.
Back on the pile, then. No coin for it, mind.
Right, that's back with me. Nothing to pay on it.

sleep._: Visible work (decision 566, npc's side): the hours a body at home lies down on its bed (Resident.activity "sleep", the lamp out). Decision 772 (Jeff: "not have npcs sleep the entire night cycle... only sleep for a 5-10 minutes each"): each body sleeps one spell of spell[0]..spell[1] game hours by its id, starting by its id between from and to less its length (Townsfolk.sleep_spell); one with no id sleeps from..to. 875 amended (2) (the coordinator's ruling on the Mughouse's evening numbers): from 23, not 21, so the evening's goers are up in the room till late; the spell's length is kept and every spell still ends by to (all up by 05:30, Rolf at his stall by 06:00).

watch._: Decision 771: the night watch. The guard captain (the first of the town's guards by id) offers a post (towns' posts, buildings') from 'from' to 'to'; one stands it within 'reach' cells of the post's rect, and one away more than 'grace_hours' in all has left it; at 'end' each who stood it is paid economy.json commissions watch_night from the treasury (what it has: 'short' when less, 'unpaid' when none) and the captain thinks the better of them (standing 'watch'). Voice's words (2026-11-02): title, words and sign_on take the post's name (%s), paid and short the gold (%d; short also what was owed).
watch.title: Stand a watch
watch.line: The town pays at first light.
watch.words: Take %s till first light; the town pays at dawn.
sign_on: Take %s. Keep the brazier lit and your eyes on the dark.
Yours is %s, till first light. Don't leave it.
Take %s, and stay there. Shout if anything comes.
paid: The night is out. The town pays you %d gold for the watch.
Dawn comes, and the watch is over. The town pays you %d gold.
First light. You are paid %d gold for the night's watch.
watch.short: First light. The town can pay you only %d of the %d gold owed for the watch.
watch.unpaid: First light. The town has no gold to pay you for the watch.
watch.left: You left your post; the town owes you nothing for tonight.
full: Every post is manned tonight. Come back tomorrow at dusk.
No posts left tonight. Try me at dusk tomorrow.
The watch is full. Tomorrow, at dusk.

waves._: 771 amended (3): the waves on a manned post. Each post draws per_night wave times a night, gap_hours apart at least, between from and to (by the town, the post and the day); at one, with its watcher at the post and none of its waves out, World.raids.wave sends 1 + the town's watchers of the post's own kinds (buildings' post data), else these kinds ({kind: weight}; dead only where a post names it). coming (by kind) is told on the first cue, and the captain comes to the post; beaten pays economy.json commissions watch_wave (beaten_short: %d paid of %d owed; beaten_unpaid none), the captain's standing watch_wave; broke when it gets past (762's threat). Voice's words (2026-11-03).

posts._: 771 amended (5): a post's own mix by its place id (Level.posts_of), in place of kinds; 'unquiet': only while the dead are unquiet (Main._dead_unquiet: the barrow's robbers not cleared, or the town's alms short; lore's crypt.dead_rise), else the night's kinds.

wolves: A howl in the dark, then another, closer. Something is coming at your post.
Eyes catch the brazier's light beyond the post. Wolves.
Howling out past the post, and coming nearer.
dead: A cold moan comes out of the dark. The dead are walking toward your post.
Shapes come out of the dark, slow and stiff. Things that should lie still are coming.
The brazier gutters, and something that should be in the ground comes toward your post.
raiders: A horn sounds out in the dark. Raiders are coming at your post.
Torches on the road, and a horn. Raiders.
Shouts and a horn beyond the post, and the sound of men running.

beaten: The last of them is down or fled. The town pays you %d gold.
Quiet again at your post. The town pays you %d gold for holding it.
You held the post. The town pays you %d gold.
beaten_short: The last of them is down or fled. The town can pay you only %d of the %d gold owed.
Quiet again at your post. The town can pay you only %d of the %d gold owed.
You held the post. The town can pay you only %d of the %d gold owed.
beaten_unpaid: The last of them is down or fled. The town has no gold to pay you.
Quiet again at your post, but the town has no gold to pay you for it.
You held the post. The town has no gold to pay you.
broke: They are past you and into the town.
They get by your post and into the lanes.
You could not hold them. They are in the town.

guard_fight._: Decision 791: guards who fight (771's next phase). A guard (Resident.FIGHTERS) is armed by trade: hp (captain_hp for the town's captain), damage (captain_damage), attack_ticks a player's (its cadence World.attack_ticks_of, the spear's speed), gear right and armour. It holds a manned post it is sent to, or the square under a threat or below fall_back_at of its hp: a foe within hold cells of that ground, never one past chase; it steps out of a tell landing within dodge_look ticks; struck, it answers where it stands for answer_ticks. It calls (call, at most every call_ticks) and the free guards within call_reach come for rally_ticks. Beaten: downed for downed_s, raised free by anyone; else laid up at the temple till back_hour after the fighting. Let be rest_ticks, it mends 1 hp every heal_every. Combat's numbers (2026-11-03); voice's words (2026-11-03).
fall_back: I'm hurt. Back to the square.
call: To me. They're at the post.
Up, all of you. They're on us.
to_post: I'm here. Hold it with me.
Stand by me and keep your feet.
guard_fight.laid_up: You were carried to the temple hurt in last night's fighting, and are off duty until tomorrow.

night._: Decision 772: where a body whose stint is home is, the night through, outside its sleep spell: by trade (else default), one pick a night by its id from [at, weight] pairs; at as the stints' (inn: the inn or tavern where the town has one, else the square). Decision 875: the default 8 inn, 1 square, 1 temple (from 6, 3, 1) while the square has nowhere to sit at night (Umbrage's inn a shell with room inside; fire seats and maps' stands to come, then the square takes more again, sitting).

_: Each trade's day, for a resident's body in its town (decisions 333 and 404): stints of {from, to, at} on DayNight's clock (hours 0-24; a stint may run over midnight), 'at' one of work, home, square, well, inn, temple; any hour no stint covers is the square, and a place the town lacks (no inn, no well, no temple standing) is the square too. A trade not listed has the default's. 'work' is where the body stands, never when economy's job runs. offset_hours: each resident's own clock runs this far ahead or behind the town's at most, by worker id, so the town never moves in lockstep. types: a hidden type's stints, over the trade's where they overlap. seasons: the day's edges move: every boundary before noon by 'morning' hours, after by 'evening'. temple: every so many days (the day by worker id), this morning hour at the temple, when the town has one. Placeholders until Jeff and economy settle each trade's day.

hearsay._: What a resident keeps of what they hear (decision 378, Hearsay): at most max claims; the newest shown believed ones reach their voice; a claims ask per resident at most every claims_ticks; a claim against what they know is believed with chance max(0, (against[0] - intellect) / against[1]), one beyond it with beyond's; a line of fewer than min_words words is never weighed.

asked._: 890: a player's question a resident's mind answers from the world's data at that moment (Main._asked_facts): kinds are word lists (lore checks them), frames the fact sentences (voice's), distances in cells.

frames.no_smith: The town has no smith now.

A word goes in only once Client3D.ACTIVITIES plays it and its prop is in. It yields nothing.

taverner._: 772 amended (2): the Mughouse's keeper keeps its counter from mid-morning into the night (the night's pick: work), abed only in its own spell.

vendor._: 853 amended (11): the stall's keeper (Rolf; Resident.day_key, his trade stays ""): his stall by day is his work (Main.INN_TRADERS_DAY), the inn at night (the night's pick).

chronicle._: Decision 491: the scholar's chronicle (TownMemory.chronicle): read at the scholar's desk (home) through the offers panel: the newest lines memories at most (the rest is in the book), and with nothing set down, lore facts of the town.

bard._: Decision 490: the bard's side-doing (Townsfolk.perform, on the gossip tick): at the inn, once a night, one piece: a town memory naming a player in the inn (told back to them once), else the newest memory not sung within again days, else lore's facts, every lore_every_nights nights at most; kinds are the words round the memory's own sentence.

gossip._: Decision 422: every 'every' steps, in each town, residents standing at one of 'places' (never at work or home) pass one thing between two of them: a belief, or something the teller saw. No model call.

lore_chars._: Decision 440: the voice's budget of lore facts by hidden type, in characters; a type not listed has Resident.LORE_CHARS (600).

settled._: Decision 471 (Jeff: 'snagfin could be an friendly goblin merchant - somewhat outcast but tolerated'): people who live in a town by name, seated at boot through economy's move_in when the town exists and they are no worker yet: id -> {name, town, trade, type, kind (the body's model), home [x, y] (a stall, not a house: the 3x3 about it), came and fact (the card's, in Jeff's words), outcast (no kin or grudge rolled)}.

snagfin.name: Snagfin
snagfin.came: came to the town from the goblins and stays, somewhat outcast but tolerated
snagfin.fact: Snagfin is a goblin among humans; the town tolerates him, which is more than most do.

rounds._: Decision 459: the lawspeaker's rounds: homes_a_day of the town's homes a day, in turn, the batch of rulings built from the people he stands with.

rulings._: Decision 448: the lawspeaker's rulings: every steps between a town's batches, rest_days before a left belief can be a candidate again, max_candidates a request, max_tokens of the answer, lore_facts given.

memory._: The town memory log (the lawspeaker, phase 1): a belief becomes a candidate for town memory once spread people have held it, held still do, and it is hold_days old; max entries kept per town.

standing._: Decision 443: what a resident thinks of a player, a score moved by events (each key a step), trusted and wronged the words' thresholds, top the last word, most the score's bound, heard what gossip moves it (to heard_most at most), why_kept reasons remembered, decay_days between steps back toward 0.

notes._: The sought's door note and the town's rumour (decision 643, npc's side; Jeff: a small note saying where they went), by story (sought.<trade>, sought.camp, economy's entry.story) over default: note takes the where-words (one %s), rumour the name, the trade and the where-words (three). Lore's lines by story come after Jeff's wording check; the defaults carry the mechanism till then. A story's own rumour (613 amended (3), the first rescue's farmer, voice's words and lore's check) says where as Towns.sought_where does, by the map's name of the refuge ("at the old farmstead"); the default keeps the where-words.

sought.farmer.camp.rumour: %s, a %s by trade, is %s, they say. We could use a hand like that here.

pointers._: Decision 837 (the coordinator's iron-slice ruling, 835's; economy's routing; voice's words, lore's check): a good a town is short of (town_sheet needs) -> the place to find it. A greeted townsperson of a town short of it says one of its lines (its town's own under towns, else lines; one a day) to a player who does not know the place yet, and the place is told them (WorldNews.tell, 805): on their map, never said to them again (Main._ore_hint).

Ore's short here. There's iron yet at Hollowfell, up in the hills, where the miners gave it up; something's moved in since.

sought._: Decision 613, npc's side (Jeff: newcomers are found in the wilds, the hills, the forest or under the castle, rescued and brought home): the sought's set lines by trade (economy's amendment keys them by the story id when it lands), _ the fallback. freed is said when the escort starts, arrival (one %s, the trade) at the town's store; held, lost and the walk are the thought's words (Resident.facts_now) through the model, bound to lore's facts. The smith's lines were agreed with lore against C3 (2026-10-22): forge_rumour, expedition, ambush.captured, forced; guards_fallen is left out while it is draft.

offers._: Decision 435 (amended 2026-10-18, Jeff): what a resident offers when spoken to: at most max fresh offers, per_player open commissions at once, a commission lapses after days. Rule: commissions come from people and what is between them, never 'go get object A from location B'; what the town is short of is talk, and banking it pays on its own; no commission needs accepting (the event completes it, with a notice and the pay).

offers._asks: Decision 536: talk with no panel. A line said to a resident that holds one of these words asks for their wares, work or news (the matching offer's words spoken back, exactly), is a yes or a no to the offer standing (a short line beginning with the word), or says an amount (a number after one of amount, or a bare number).

mood._note: A companion resting in town shows her mood toward her player (decision 555, npc's side; companions write mood and mood_why on her worker record). apart_at: where she sits alone instead of her trade while the mood is apart (a whereabouts place: well, inn, square, temple). Sullen or apart, the town's gossip notes once a day that she is unhappy with her player, companions' reason verbatim.
